messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Stan print progress
parts:
In the new code, we print progress of warmup and sampling separately.  Is this our intended behavior?  This is an example:

$ ./dogs --iter=10 --data=dogs.data.R
STAN SAMPLING COMMAND
......
delta = 0.5
gamma = 0.05
Iteration: 1 / 5 [ 20%]  (Warmup)
Iteration: 2 / 5 [ 40%]  (Warmup)
Iteration: 3 / 5 [ 60%]  (Warmup)
Iteration: 4 / 5 [ 80%]  (Warmup)
Iteration: 5 / 5 [100%]  (Warmup)
Iteration: 1 / 5 [ 20%]  (Sampling)
Iteration: 2 / 5 [ 40%]  (Sampling)
Iteration: 3 / 5 [ 60%]  (Sampling)
Iteration: 4 / 5 [ 80%]  (Sampling)
Iteration: 5 / 5 [100%]  (Sampling)

Elapsed Time: 0.003949 seconds (Warm Up)
              0.010438 seconds (Sampling)
              0.014387 seconds (Total)

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan print progress
parts:
Is there an equivalent of std::endl for carriage return?

It used to overwrite, but then I went back to just writing
out one at a time due to portability issues.

Right now, we have std::endl in command-line code,
which generates platform-specific output. But we
have "\n" hard-coded into the code generator and
into our output file generation to standardize on
unix-style newlines.


- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan print progress
parts: Nope - iostreams are literally streams and don't implement the functionality required for carriage return (which would require more integration into the terminal environment). \r works on Windows and some Linux boxes but it's not guaranteed. It looks like ncurses is the only library that enables carriage-return functionality on most systems, but it also does so with significantly more overhead than iostreams.
